q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT b.name AS beer, COALESCE(MIN(s.price), NULL) AS price, COALESCE(ba.name, NULL) AS bar FROM beer AS b LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.beer LEFT JOIN bar AS ba ON ba.name = s.bar AND s.price > (SELECT MIN(price) FROM serves WHERE beer = b.name) GROUP BY b.name, ba.name ORDER BY b.name

But that's not the same as the actual minimum price of the beer. 

So Q1 is correctly getting the minimum price and the bar where it's served. Q2, on the other hand, is selecting the minimum price that is greater than the actual minimum, which would be the second lowest price. Wait, but the SELECT in Q2 is COALESCE(MIN(s.price), NULL) as price. However, if there are no serves that meet the condition (s.price > min), then MIN would be NULL, and COALESCE would return NULL. But that's not the same as the actual min price. So Q2 is not getting the minimum price, but the minimum of the prices that are higher than the minimum. Which is incorrect.

Then MIN(s.price) is 3, so Q2 would return 3 as the price. But the actual minimum is 2, so Q2 is wrong here.
